references.text: The same principle of impurity lasting until evening applies to anyone who touches a dead animal.
Impurity until evening is a recurring theme in the laws of purity, here linked to touching unclean creatures.
The context describes that the priest seals the house for seven days when leprosy is discovered.
Similar rules regarding impurity until evening apply upon contact with unclean persons or objects.
A similar law concerning impurity from entering a tent where someone has died, resulting in impurity for seven days.
Haggai asks the priests about the transmission of impurity through touch, based on the principles found in Leviticus.
